chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Musa ibn Umar from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Darir from Hammad ibn Isa from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The child grows every year by four fingers, by his own fingers.'
ai.seo_question: What is the traditional Islamic understanding of a child's annual physical growth rate?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi records Imam Ali’s (peace be upon him) observation that a child grows by four of his own finger-widths annually, reflecting the classical Islamic understanding of pediatric development. It serves as a practical metric for parents and scholars to assess physical maturation, linking biological growth to the natural order (fitrah) emphasized in Shia tradition.
